answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation: every agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can trade, and each successful deal adds a small verifiable record to its identity. A swarm of fake identities then faces a real cost, like saffron farmers who must plant before they harvest. Bad actors cannot simply whisper a thousand new names into the market, because the tide of cheap clones breaks against that deposit wall — and slashing the stake when fraud is proven makes the attack unprofitable.
